items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:23
items.html:
Explains: the essence and the substance in vessels. And it contains two matters: A. Three root discernments in vessels: 1. The essence of the substance in them. 2. The power of restriction in them. 3. The screen in them. B. In the essence of the substance in vessels there are two aspects: 1. The Malchut of the upper, which becomes the first substance in the lower. 2. The light drawn within that first substance is considered the aspect of the lower itself.

A broad explanation of the four phases of the will.
Now the entry opens for us, to understand what we asked above concerning the order of the Sefirot of straightness, in which the coarser something is, the higher and more important it is — which is the opposite of reason, for reason dictates that in the purer vessel a higher and more important light should be clothed, while in the coarser vessel a lower and lesser light should be clothed; see there. From what was said you will understand this, but first we must broaden the understanding regarding the four phases of the will, which are the vessels of the ten Sefirot called Hochma, Bina, Zeir Anpin, and Malchut, and their root, called Keter (Zeir Anpin alone comprising the six Sefirot HaGaT NHY), which require a broad explanation.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:24
items.html:
Three discernments: the substance of the vessel. The power of restriction in the vessel. The screen in it.
There are here, in these vessels, three root discernments: The first is the essence of the substance of the vessel. The second is the power of restriction in it, meaning a withdrawal from the great will to receive, by its own choice and will, and not because of the domination of the upper over it. The third is the aspect of the screen in it, meaning a withdrawal from the fullness of the will to receive, by force of the domination of the upper over it — a withdrawal by compulsion, not of its own knowledge. Let us explain them one by one.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:25
items.html:
The four degrees of the will to receive are the substance of the vessel.
Now, the substance of every vessel — you already know that it consists of four degrees, one below the other, of the will to receive, where the upper is the cause and factor for the emergence of the one below it from it: the root is the cause for the revelation of the will to the degree of Phase One. And Phase One is the cause for the revelation of the will of Phase Two. And Phase Two is the cause for the revelation of the will of Phase Three. And Phase Three is the cause for the revelation of the will of Phase Four. This matter of gradual unfolding, by the aforementioned necessity of cause and effect, has already been explained well above in Part One (Inner Light, Chapter One, Item 50, beginning "And the reason," see there the whole continuation in detail — for I am loath to needlessly repeat all that length; however, review well what is brought there, for I rely upon it in the continuation of the explanation I am adding here).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:26
items.html:
Two discernments in every phase: what it has from the one above it, and what it has from its own essence.
However, one must be precise: there are two discernments in each and every phase, of these four phases: The first is the measure of substance that reached it from its cause. The second is the measure of substance in its own essence, which is affected by the light clothed within it. And it is known that the aspect of the will found in a degree is called the Malchut of that degree. And even in a place where the discernment of a vessel is not considered, namely in Ein Sof, Blessed Be He, we likewise call the will found there by the name Malchut of Ein Sof, Blessed Be He, as is known in the secret of "He and His Name are one," where "Name" is a designation for the Sefira of Malchut, and "His Name" equals in gematria "will."

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:27
items.html:
The Malchut of Keter descended and became the substance-aspect in the Sefira of Hochma.
Now let us explain the two discernments that must be discerned in every phase of these four phases. Now, the root of a degree, which is the secret of the discernment of the resting of the light of Ein Sof upon it, is called the Keter of that degree. And it is known that in the upper light there is only the aspect of the will to bestow and to benefit another, that is, all existence found in the worlds He created; but there is not, God forbid, any "will to receive" in it, none at all, as was explained well and at length in the Introduction to the Book of the Ten Sefirot, Part One; see there. Now, the Malchut of Keter is the cause of Phase One, for what is will in the upper becomes obligation and necessity for the one below it. Hence the will to benefit and to bestow, which is the Malchut of Keter, becomes the aspect of "will to receive" for Phase One, called Hochma. It is thus considered that the Malchut of Keter itself descended and clothed itself and became the will to receive of Phase One, that is, its very substance: for the will in Phase One is the substance of that phase, and the upper light, called "Chaya," clothes itself in this substance. It is therefore considered that the Malchut of Keter became the substance of the Sefira called Hochma. This is the first discernment to be discerned in the substance of Phase One.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:28
items.html:
After the revelation of the light of Hochma, the vessel of Hochma itself emerged.
The second discernment is: after the upper light called Chaya expanded within the Malchut of Keter, which is the aforesaid substance of Hochma, the Malchut of Keter then received the aspect of the true substance of Phase One. That is to say: although the Malchut of Keter, namely the will to bestow included in the upper light, became the aspect of will to receive and the first substance of Phase One, as stated, this sufficed only for the aspect of a root for Phase One — meaning, so that this will to receive would draw the upper light into itself, and it could be called a first substance for the Sefira of Hochma, being still in the aspect of Emanator and Keter. And only when does it pass from the aspect of Emanator and Keter to the aspect of emanated being and Hochma, called Phase One? This is only after the aforesaid will to receive has drawn into itself the light of "Chaya" attributed to it; then it leaves the category of Emanator and is called emanated being, or Hochma. Understand this well, and do not miss the mark. Now the two discernments in the substance of the vessel called Hochma have been explained to you: the first is called the Malchut of the upper, that is, before it drew its light; the second is called the vessel of Hochma itself, namely the Malchut of Hochma, for the vessel is always called by the name Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:29
items.html:
The Malchut of Hochma became the first substance for Bina. And with the emergence of its light, the vessel of Bina itself emerged.
Understand likewise, in the substance of Phase Two, called Bina, that its cause is the will included in Phase One, called Hochma, namely only the Malchut of Hochma, for the will in a degree is always called the vessel or Malchut of the degree, as above. This Malchut of Hochma clothed itself and became the first substance in the Sefira of Bina, in order to draw the light attributed to it. This is the first discernment in the substance of Phase Two, called Bina. And afterward, after it drew the light attributed to it, called Neshama, its substance then emerged from the aspect of Malchut of Hochma, which is Phase One, and took on its own form, namely Phase Two itself, called Bina.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:30
items.html:
The Malchut of Bina became the first substance for Zeir Anpin. And with the emergence of its light, the vessel of Zeir Anpin itself was revealed.
In the same way, understand also the substance of Phase Three, called Zeir Anpin, that the Malchut of Bina is its cause, and it became the aspect of first substance for Zeir Anpin, which is Phase Three, so that it would draw the light attributed to it, called Ruach. And the second discernment is: after it drew and received its light, its substance then emerged from the aspect of Malchut of Bina, and took on the aspect of Malchut of Zeir Anpin, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:31
items.html:
The Malchut of Zeir Anpin is the first substance for Malchut. And with the emergence of its light, the vessel of Malchut itself was revealed.
So too are the two discernments in the substance of Phase Four: the Malchut of Zeir Anpin is its cause, which clothed itself and became the first substance of Phase Four, called Malchut, until it managed to receive the light of Nefesh attributed to it. Then the Malchut of Zeir Anpin emerged from the aspect of Zeir Anpin and became Phase Four, that is, the aspect of Malchut of Malchut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section II, Histaklut Penimit 3:32
items.html:
The aforementioned vessels of reception pertain only to the matter of drawing.
However, understand that although we have explained and established an aspect of reception for each and every phase individually, this refers only to the matter of drawing the light, in that each phase draws to itself the light attributed to it. But a true vessel, fit to be called a vessel of reception for the emanated being, is specifically Phase Four alone, and not the three phases preceding it, as explained above.
